lead: eleven friendships, and you could name the evening each one stopped being interesting. none of them ended. they are all still housed, still on the list, still yours, and the wanting-to-know ran out years before the arrangement did.
sun: what you put up does not come down when the reason for it does. somebody got interesting for a season, came under, and a cover has no setting for withdrawing itself from someone already inside — so twelve years on they still have the room, the money when needed, the phone answered at two, all of it running on an interest that ended in the second year and was never announced.
moon: the searching face goes out at each new one and has the whole of them inside three evenings, which is why the recruiting is fast and the roster is long. it has never been turned around. nobody has come at you the way you go at them, because the interesting part of you is under the cover, and a covered thing gives off nothing for anyone to follow.
pull: eleven people were found out inside a fortnight each. none has ever gone looking for you — the cover was up the whole time, and nothing about it invites the question.
tension: they call it loyalty and the evidence is good: nobody has been dropped, nobody let go quietly over a year of unanswered messages. what they cannot see is that the interest stopped and the cover did not, so each year the choice is between housing somebody you are bored of and putting a person outside. you take the first one every time. the boredom is what you are keeping from them, and the affection was never the secret.
cost: somebody gets a permanent place off you on the strength of one good evening, with nothing to qualify for and no review at any point after. each of those places rests on one interested person who stopped being interested, and the eleven of them have no idea they are standing on a season that ended, because the underside of it has never been shown to anybody.

lead: a hundred people watched you take a man apart at a meeting, and the reason is somebody who cannot be named in that room or any other. both are permanent. only one is on the record.
sun: everything that would explain that evening is under something you put up. the woman it was about is still under it, and producing her would be the same act as taking the cover off her. so the scene stands in the open with nothing behind it. the hall got the event entire and the cause not at all, which is the arrangement working as built, for the first time against you.
moon: the mark left in that room does not thin out. it is four minutes old, finished, and it will be on you at that size in twenty years. the cover is the same sum pointed the other way: nothing spent yet, one point of contact, and when it goes it goes whole. one of them has already happened once and for all. the other has that still to do.
pull: four minutes, spent, permanent. the cover, unspent, standing on one point, permanent in the other direction. you are underneath both, and the hall has seen one.
tension: the people who could say what you are like are the people whose presence is the thing that cannot be said. so the account of you in that town got assembled in one evening by a hundred witnesses who were all there, and it is accurate about the event and wrong about the man, and every correction costs somebody their cover. you have been going to the same meetings for three years underneath it, which reads to them as brass.
cost: a verdict from a hundred people lands on you and the work under it continues at full strength for years, with the mitigating fact never once produced. the version they hold has set. he is entitled to his account of that evening and gives it freely, and the thing that would settle it is a person who has to keep sleeping somewhere, so it stays unsettled and it stays yours.

lead: it went back up in a fortnight and by the second week everyone was under it again at the trust they had before, which is the wrong amount, and correcting it would mean saying what happened the first time.
sun: the nine years have no stated cause. what took it down was one bad year of yours, and that year has never been available for inspection, so the people who were suddenly outside filed it as a move, or a job, or a marriage going wrong — the ordinary reasons, supplied by them, uncorrected by you. the cover went on doing its work while it was flat on the ground with nobody under it.
moon: what comes back does not have to be re-founded. four messages and the whole thing was running by the second thursday, same people, no ceremony about the gap, nobody asking for an account of where it went. recovery is the native expectation here and the expectation was met, which is how a collapse gets filed at both ends as an interval, including at your end, where the facts are.
pull: nine years down, a fortnight to put back, and nothing that needed explaining — the thing nobody asked about is the thing that will do it again.
tension: the return is now evidence. it survived nine years off, so it is the kind of thing that survives — that is the sentence they are running on, and it reverses what took place. a second point of contact would have to be justified out loud, and the justification is under there with everything else, so what stands over them now is the same single upright, carrying more people, with a decade of proof behind it that it holds.
cost: you can restore a thing whole after nine years with no re-explaining, no founding meeting, nobody having to be persuaded twice. what did not get rebuilt is anything about how it stands, because the case for building differently is the year you will not describe, and everyone who walked back in did so on a record that has the collapse listed as a pause.

lead: three years on, his wife still rings you most weeks and his mother rings on the anniversary, and neither of them knows what he was to you. nor did he. the shopping gets done either way.
sun: the household he left is upright because you got something over it in the first week — the school run, the bills, the room his aunt sleeps in. what nobody inside it has is any part of what he was to you. it was not available before he died and is not now, and the arrangement is the reason: whoever is doing the covering does not get to be one of the people under it.
moon: nobody in that house can say how much of it comes from you, and nobody outside it has been given anything to look at. at the distance most people stand, you are somebody who was fond of him and has been kind since. up close there is a whole family running on a supply with no meter on it, and the rate has not moved once in three years.
pull: you are the second person that death happened to, in a house full of the first, and your share of him is the one thing under there that has never been set out.
tension: grief has a running order and yours has no place in it. the wife gets the visits, the sister gets the calls, and you get asked how they are all holding up, warmly, by people who are not wrong about who has the first claim. the answer would start with what he was to you, and that has been under cover for eleven years, from them, from her, and from him while he was alive to hear it.
cost: five people came through the year after a death with the bills paid and the fridge full and no one of them having to ask. under there with them is a man you have never had anywhere to put down, and one point holds the whole thing, so a bad winter of yours arrives in that house as the death happening to them a second time.
